subject: Capacity sizing & lead-time dependencies for MAP - Cumulus AI
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cumulus.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cumulus AI Procurement <procurement@cumulus.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff + capacity constraints (Cumulus AI)

Marcus — thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement here; we want to lock a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes explicit capacity reservation windows and lead-time assumptions for both Redwood Dedicated and a potential Private (on‑prem/VPC) deployment.

High level ask: we need a clear timeline and sizing proposal that we can take through our internal procurement + infra approval (SRE) by end of Q4. Key constraints on our side:
- Production burst pattern: 1.5M tokens/day steady, spikes up to 5M tokens/day for 2–6 hours daily.
- Preference for H100-class instances for critical low-latency endpoints, A100 or equivalent acceptable for less latency-sensitive workloads.
- Security: Private deployment is preferred for sensitive pipelines but will require a longer procurement window.

Can you lay out: 1) lead-time for Dedicated capacity (typical procurement-to-live), 2) lead-time for Private (on‑prem/VPC) deployment, 3) a recommended pool sizing for an initial MAP (pilot + production tranches), and 4) acceptance criteria we should include in the MAP?

Attached is our current MAP draft (Cumulus-MAP-v2.docx) and a rough utilization snapshot.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m to walk through if easier.

— Alex Chen
Director, Platform Engineering
Cumulus AI
procurement@cumulus.ai

Attachments: Cumulus-MAP-v2.docx (docx), capacity-snapshot.csv (csv)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cumulus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + capacity constraints (Cumulus AI)

Alex — great summary, thanks. I pulled together a short, pragmatic plan below so you can present something concrete to procurement + SRE. Happy to jump on a call; I'm free tomorrow morning.

Summary recommendations (pilot → production tranches):
- Pilot (8 weeks): 4 x H100-equivalent slots (low-latency endpoints), 8 x A100-equivalent burst pool for background batch/embedding jobs. Purpose: smoke test production prompts, validate KV cache behavior, warm prefix caching.
- Production tranche (steady state after pilot, target t+16 weeks from PO): 32 x H100-equivalent (serving), 64 x A100-equivalent (batch/replication) — can be staged in 2 x 16 blocks across two regions.

Lead-time assumptions (typical):
- Redwood Dedicated: procurement-to-live 6–10 weeks for reserved pools (if using available cloud inventory and regional capacity). Shorter if customer accepts best-effort placement vs guaranteed tranche timings.
- Private (VPC/on‑prem): 12–20 weeks depending on hardware lead time, networking vlan/KMS onboarding, and customer procurement cadence. On‑prem can be longer if hardware ordering is needed (H100 inventory variability).

Acceptance criteria for MAP (suggested checklist):
- Pilot readiness: pilot pool available, smoke endpoints reachable from Cumulus SRE, example prompts within latency SLO (p95 target), prefix cache warmed scripts executed.
- Data controls: KMS keys configured, logging/audit hooks confirmed, SOC2 logs accessible to Red team (per MAP doc).
- Failover: fallback routing to smaller hosted model variant (if Dedicated unavailable) validated.
- Performance targets: p50/p95/p99 latency targets per endpoint, token throughput baseline validated with your traffic patterns.

Operational notes / options:
- Staggered tranches reduce lead-time risk; we can lock an initial smaller Dedicated tranche quickly and then expand in commit windows.
- If you need strict calendar dates for lead times in the MAP, we'll put a firm SLA addendum into the Dedicated contract (extra cost for guaranteed capacity reservation).

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal alignment (Ben/Naomi/Priyom): confirm feasibility and any constraints on our side (inventory, SLA addendum cadence).
2) Marcus to provide a one‑page MAP appendix with explicit weeks for milestones (pilot start, production tranche 1, tranche 2).
3) Align on acceptance tests and a shared runbook for on‑ramp / cutover.

I attached a quick capacity snapshot we use internally (capacity-snapshot.csv) and the Redwood Dedicated SLA reference (redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf).

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: capacity-snapshot.csv (csv), redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf (pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MAP kickoff + capacity constraints (Cumulus AI) — internal alignment

Forwarding Alex's note — he wants firm lead-times and a MAP appendix we can ship to procurement. Quick internal Qs / asks: please reply inline with short bullets.

1) Inventory risk: can we guarantee H100-class availability for a 32-slot tranche across two regions in a T+16 week window? If not, what are realistic alternatives?
2) Private/on‑prem: what is our standard timeline if customer provides racks vs if we need to source hardware?
3) Cost / SLA: for a guaranteed calendar window, what uplift do we need to attach to the SLA addendum?

Notes from my side:
- If inventory is tight, recommend a hybrid: lock 16 guaranteed H100s and allow flexible placement for the remainder (quantized grace windows).
- For Private where customer supplies racks, timeline is closer to 10–14 weeks (networking + KMS onboarding is largest chunk). If Redwood sources HW, 14–20 weeks due to lead time.

Ben / Priyom / Naomi — please drop short replies today so I can author the MAP appendix and return to Alex with dates.

— Marcus

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cumulus.ai>

Cc: Cumulus AI Procurement <procurement@cumulus.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + capacity constraints (Cumulus AI)

Marcus — this looks good and aligns to our internal thinking. A few clarifications from procurement/SRE after a quick sync:

- Pilot: we can accept 4 x H100 + 8 x A100 for 8 weeks. We want pilot start no later than 2026-12-15 to meet our internal release window.
- Production tranche: given vendor cycles, we prefer the 2 x 16-staging approach across two AZs / regions. Our procurement target for tranche 1 is 2027-03-01; tranche 2 to follow no earlier than 2027-06-01.
- Private/on‑prem: we'll commit to providing racks + basic L2/L3 networking within 8 weeks of PO — if Redwood needs to source HW, we estimate +6–8 weeks on top of that.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood produce a MAP appendix with explicit calendar dates (pilot start, tranche1 target, tranche2 target) and an acceptance-test checklist we can include in the contract?
2) We want an optional SLA addendum quote for guaranteed calendar reservation for tranche 1 (if Redwood can firm dates earlier than typical).

I'll attach an updated internal slate to the MAP doc and share procurement notes.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — if you can get the appendix this week, we'll circulate to SRE and procurement.

— Alex

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + capacity constraints (Cumulus AI) — MAP appendix and next steps

Alex — attached is the one‑page MAP appendix and a short acceptance checklist (see links below). Key commitments:

- Pilot start target: 2026-12-15 (subject to PO signature + onboarding tasks). Pilot = 4x H100, 8x A100, 8-week window.
- Production tranche 1 target: 2027-03-01 (32x H100-equivalent in 2x16 blocks across two regions). Option to accelerate to an earlier calendar date with SLA addendum.
- Production tranche 2 target: 2027-06-01 (scale to 64x A100-equivalent for batch capacity).

Acceptance checklist highlights:
- Network reachability & KMS: 3 tests (SRE exec checklist)
- Latency SLO smoke: run our p95 script; baseline must meet target for core endpoints
- Failover test: route 10% of traffic to fallback hosted variant for 1 hour without errors
- Security evidence: provide SOC2 export + access to audit logs in the shared drive link

Operational notes and options:
- If Cumulus wants guaranteed calendar reservations for tranche 1, Redwood can provide an SLA addendum (4–8% uplift on committed monthly fees depending on region). That buy gives a firm placement window and financial penalties if Redwood misses the committed dates.
- If hardware sourcing is on Cumulus, we can compress Private timeline to ~10–14 weeks; if Redwood sources, expect ~14–20 weeks.

Links:
- MAP appendix (draft): https://redwoodapp.atlassian.net/browse/RED-4532
- HubSpot record: HubSpot:HS-987654321

Ben/Priyom/Naomi — I used the conservative timeline you flagged. If anything here looks risky from an ops perspective, call it out and I'll push a variant to Alex immediately.

Next steps:
1) Alex reviews appendix and acceptance checklist.
2) Alex confirms PO timing and whether Cumulus will provide racks or needs Redwood sourcing.
3) If Cumulus wants guaranteed dates, Ben to price SLA addendum; Priyom to confirm inventory uplift.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: MAP_appendix_onepage.pdf (pdf)
